recentItems.title: Mada Masr’s Lina Attalah due to appear before court in Egypt
recentItems.description:
Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah is set to face a retrial before an Egyptian criminal court on Wednesday, after being sentenced in absentia to one year in prison for operating an unlicensed website and spreading ‘false news’. The court has also ordered the closure of the independent news outlet.

recentItems.title: Palestinian Grandmother, 72, Killed by Israeli Settler in Occupied West Bank
recentItems.description:
A 72-year-old Palestinian grandmother, Faddah Fheidat, has been shot and killed by an Israeli settler in Al Dyuk Al Tahta, near Jericho in the occupied West Bank.

Her son was also shot and arrested by Israeli forces, while witnesses dispute the allegations against him.

Al Jazeera's Nida Ibrahim reports on the family's loss and growing concerns over escalating settler violence and the lack of accountability.

recentItems.title: Trump, Putin and Xi: Historic three-way meeting in China
recentItems.description:
Donald Trump has arrived in China for the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, ahead of a highly anticipated trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The unprecedented meeting is expected to address major international issues, including nuclear non-proliferation, the war in Ukraine and global security. Trump has also suggested that discussions could touch on Iran and North Korea.

Before Trump's arrival, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin held talks in Shenzhen, reaffirming their close strategic partnership. Both leaders called for a more multipolar world order and stronger cooperation amid growing international uncertainty.

But the meeting comes against a backdrop of tensions between Washington and Beijing over trade tariffs, technology competition, Taiwan and regional security.

Al Jazeera correspondent Katrina Yu reports from Shenzhen on China's diplomatic ambitions, Putin's growing international engagement and the significance of Trump's latest visit.

While some countries see the trilateral talks as an opportunity for greater international cooperation, European leaders are concerned about the implications for Ukraine and the future of Western alliances.

Can this meeting reshape global diplomacy, or will longstanding rivalries prevent meaningful progress?
